title: Directional complex-root sampling and common-band payment
analyticClaims: For real or complex Banach-valued X in W^{2,1}, the squared derivative mass at all selected roots except the first is at most twice the integral of ||X'|| ||X''||.
The factor two is sharp and the first-root payment is necessary.
For the declared perturbative common-band triangular class, the complete complex-target root mass is comparable to a^2 N^2 and its physical critical-log normalization tends to zero.
finiteDiagnostics: Seven exact rational sharpness cases approach the factor-two boundary.
Producer and independent R0.72K routes transform separately archived R0.72J row data at R=4,8,16,32,64.
No new PDE time evolution is performed for this figure.
claimBoundary: The abstract sampling lemma and common-band theorem are proved analytically in research/r072k_report-source.md. The finite points are implementation and lineage checks, not an interval proof, root enumeration, continuation theorem, singularity construction, or general Navier-Stokes regularity result.
